candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Convert mixed numbers (and whole numbers when needed) into equivalent improper fractions (or equivalent fractions with a specified denominator) to enable fraction operations.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three experts define the same conversion operation: rewriting a mixed number a b/c as (a·c+b)/c and optionally rewriting whole numbers as fractions to match a needed denominator.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Determine a common denominator (often via LCM) and rewrite each fraction as an equivalent fraction over that denominator by scaling numerator and denominator.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three experts include both parts of the concept: selecting/finding a common denominator (often LCM) and converting each fraction to an equivalent form with that denominator.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Compute the difference of two rational numbers once in compatible form, typically by subtracting numerators over a common denominator and/or subtracting whole and fractional parts separately and combining.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: Expert C names it 'Subtract aligned fractions' but the definition and criteria match A/B: perform the subtraction after alignment (same denominator or decomposed whole/fraction parts), excluding mere conversion or simplification.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Express the computed result in simplest accepted form by reducing fractions and/or converting between improper fractions, mixed numbers, and integers as appropriate.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three experts describe the same post-computation finishing step: reduce to lowest terms and optionally convert improper↔mixed or to an integer, explicitly excluding the subtraction/common-denominator steps.

alignment_summary: Across A, B, and C, the skill sets are isomorphic: each codebook contains the same four concepts (convert mixed/whole to improper/equivalent fractions, find a common denominator and rewrite, perform subtraction in compatible form, and simplify/convert the final result). Naming differences are minor (notably C's 'Subtract aligned fractions'), and all concepts have full 3/3 consensus with one-to-one mappings.
